Class Item3D

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.mdi3D.item3D.Item3D
Direct Known Subclasses:
Axes3D, Cube, Cylinder, GlobeCountryLines3D, LabelSet3D, Line3D, PointSet3D, PolyLine3D, Quad3D, ScatterPlot3D, Sphere, Triangle3D
public abstract class Item3D extends Object
Base class for every drawable object hosted on a Panel3D.

Item3D is the 3D analogue of MDI's 2D AItem: a self-contained drawable that owns its own appearance properties and can be organized into a parent/child tree so a group of items (e.g. the axes of a coordinate frame, or the components of a composite shape) can be shown, hidden, or disposed as a unit.

Properties

Appearance is stored as a small Properties-backed key/value bag (LINE_WIDTH, FILLCOLOR, FILLALPHA, LINECOLOR, LINEALPHA, TEXT_COLOR, FONT), accessed through the typed get*/set* convenience methods. Any property that has not been explicitly set falls back to a class-wide default.

Drawing and disposal

Subclasses implement draw(GLAutoDrawable) for their own custom rendering, and only that GL-thread-bound method should touch the GL context. drawItem(GLAutoDrawable) and disposeItem(GLAutoDrawable) are called by Panel3D and are final: they invoke draw(GLAutoDrawable)/dispose(GLAutoDrawable) on this item and then recurse into every visible child, so a subtree draws or releases its GL resources with a single call from the panel.

Thread safety

isVisible()/setVisible(boolean) and the child list are safe to touch from threads other than the GL rendering thread: visibility is volatile, and addChild(Item3D)/removeChild(Item3D) synchronize on this, the same monitor used to snapshot the child list before iterating it during draw/dispose. Actual GL calls inside draw(GLAutoDrawable) still must only happen on the GL thread.

    • disposeItem

      public final void disposeItem(com.jogamp.opengl.GLAutoDrawable drawable)
      Called by the panel3D when its GL context is being torn down. Do not overwrite.

      Releases this item's own GL resources via dispose(GLAutoDrawable), then recurses into children so a subtree is fully released with one call.

      Parameters:
      drawable - the OpenGL drawable being disposed

    • dispose

      protected void dispose(com.jogamp.opengl.GLAutoDrawable drawable)
      Override to release any GL resources this item owns (textures, display lists, text renderers, etc.).

      The default implementation does nothing. Items that lazily allocate GL-backed resources — for example a JOGL TextRenderer — should override this to release them and null out the field so a subsequent draw call (if any) lazily recreates it.

      Parameters:
      drawable - the OpenGL drawable being disposed

    • addChild

      public void addChild(Item3D item)
      Add a child item.

      The remove-then-add (to move an existing child to the end) is performed under synchronized(this) so it is atomic with respect to childrenSnapshot() — a concurrent drawer/disposer can never observe the child transiently missing.

      Parameters:
      item - the child item
